title: MASTER PLAN v2 — Anchor steward: campaign orchestration by conversation
claims: This planning session produced the approved Master Plan v2 for the "Anchor steward" effort — the feature that will let John run an entire multi-stage project campaign through conversation with a steward that proposes, waits for confirmation, and commissions the trio skills (researchPrime, Crucible, Foreman) rather than doing the work itself. Working under the locked North Star v4, the session revised the earlier nine-phase draft into an eleven-phase plan that reflects what a verified intake audit found already built: the existing Ecgberht commission machinery, brief packet, and portfolio index are now audited for wiring fitness (with a handful of named defects, like a stale-cache key and a non-atomic confirm write, recorded as fix items) instead of being rebuilt, while the genuinely missing piece — an Anchor-side executor that takes a confirmed commission and drives a real trio run — is scheduled as new Wave-1 work. The plan's central spending rule was reshaped into a "confirmed compile envelope": John confirms one bounded session budget up front, every compile is still individually shown, exhaustion is a hard stop, and unattended reflections queue rather than spend. Two new phases were added — a Rehydration phase, so that after killing everything and returning days later the steward opens with an accurate wake-up brief that names dead runs and re-asks nothing already answered, and an Attention/High Seat phase giving each project a typed attention state and a portfolio-at-a-glance view served from the existing index. The plan culminates in a demo-as-acceptance-test: one end-to-end campaign, run with auth on, that exercises all thirteen North Star criteria including a mid-demo kill and recovery. Every phase carries mechanical gates and explicit failure-state tables, and the trio skill internals remain fenced off from modification throughout.

This planning session produced the approved Stage-1 Master Plan (v2) for the Anchor steward effort — the "campaign orchestration by conversation" project, in which the Ecgberht steward runs multi-stage project campaigns through typed conversation, commissioning the trio skills (researchPrime, Crucible, Foreman) rather than reimplementing them. The plan was revised from the earlier nine-phase draft to incorporate John's locked Stage-1 edits and was approved on 2026-07-31 against the locked North Star v4, with every phase explicitly mapped to the thirteen numbered criteria. The session reshaped the plan in several important ways: the old rebuild-style gate on the commission machinery was shrunk to a wiring audit of the already-built Ecgberht halves (with any defects treated as fix items, never re-plans), while genuinely new work was re-aimed at the verified-absent Anchor side — a minimal commission executor that drives a confirmed commission through Anchor's real job substrate to an observed process and returned handback. It also adopted the confirmed compile envelope as the canonical spend model (John confirms one bounded budget per session covering compiles and stage-boundary reflections, with exhaustion a hard stop and unattended reflections queued rather than spent), and added two new phases: a Rehydration phase that assembles a wake-up brief from the ledger after a full kill so the steward resumes with no re-asked questions, and an Attention/High Seat phase delivering a typed attention projection, badge, and portfolio-at-a-glance served from the already-built portfolio index. The result is an eleven-phase plan — running from ground-truth audits and a single-writer ledger spine, through an ugly-but-real vertical slice, the compiled Face, steward-authored scaffolding, hardened launch and handback validation, up to a final end-to-end campaign demo that doubles as the acceptance test — each phase carrying mechanical gates, failure-state tables, and standing rules that fence the trio and portfolio-index code from modification.
